To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coupling index and damping values are two parameters that can be used to control the pressure field within the combustion chamber.
the premixer can be considered acoustically decouple from the chamber if the acoustic coupling index is lower than a critical value.

the acoustic reflection coefficients of the premixing section are key parameters to control the pressure field in the combustor and that a good knowledge of the damping values in the different sections of the combustor is necessary to determine whether the system is decoupled or not.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an experimental methodology for the study of acoustics in gas turbine combustion systems, and the development of a numerical model to predict the sound pressure field and the acoustic modes of a combustion system.
a new methodology that enables to predict the coupling between two acoustically coupled cavities and the corresponding pressure distribution.
a detailed analysis of the acoustic coupling between a premixer and a combustion chamber, and the effects of the acoustic coupling on the flame dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acoustic coupling index is not sufficient to predict the coupling between the premixer and combustor.
the acoustic coupling of the premixer to the combustion chamber can be avoided by either adjusting the impedance of the premixer or the damping of the combustion chamber.

the acoustic decoupling of cavities can be achieved either through the modification of the damping values featuring a given frequency or through the modification of both the coupling index and the damping values featuring different frequencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coupling index is the most important parameter to consider when designing a combustion chamber.
the acoustic coupling index is an effective tool to predict the coupling between cavities and that the damping of the cavities plays a key role when frequencies are close to match.
the coupling index and damping of the system are the key parameters to predict whether the premixer and chamber are acoustically coupled or not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acoustic impedance of the premixer is an important parameter to control the acoustic behavior of the coupled-cavities system.
the acoustic coupling between cavities is not only a matter of the acoustic impedance at the interfaces but also of the damping of both cavities.
the coupling index and the damping values are the two key parameters for predicting the coupling between cavities, and therefore, the acoustic field in the system.
